work.name: Cyber Interface Laboratory, The University of Tokyo
work.summary: Conducting research on virtual self-modeling, social plausibility, and memory integration in mixed reality environments.
highlights: Studying human-avatar interaction and plausibility perception using HMDs with video see-through capabilities.
Designing VR experiments exploring empathy, trust, and self-projection in behavioral change contexts.

work.name: Apple Camp / Today at Apple
work.summary: Led creative coding and digital art sessions using iPad and Swift Playgrounds for young learners.
highlights: Taught participants to express ideas through interactive media and visual storytelling.

work.name: Visual Media Laboratory, Tokyo City University
work.summary: Conducted research on reducing VR sickness through peripheral motion line effects using Unity and ARKit.
highlights: Developed iOS AR prototypes and Unity-based VR experiments for perceptual analysis.
Published results as part of undergraduate thesis and cross-institutional collaboration.

education.area: Interdisciplinary Information Studies (Emerging Design and Informatics Course)

awards.title: Outstanding Graduate Award
awards.summary: Recognized for academic excellence and research achievement.

awards.title: Exchange Program Research Achievement Recognition
awards.summary: Awarded for research contribution to VR sickness reduction study.

projects.name: The You You Are
projects.summary: An interactive installation enabling real-time conversations with a 'parallel self' through AI and voice cloning, exploring identity and self-reflection.

projects.name: 28 Xiu / 28 Mansions
projects.summary: An AR application visualizing the Chinese lunar mansions using RealityKit and SwiftUI, integrating cultural storytelling and astronomical visualization.

projects.name: Collaborative Avatars for Motivation
projects.summary: A VR experiment investigating how observing one's avatar being praised affects motivation and self-perception.

projects.name: Weak Virtual Agent Project
projects.summary: A research project exploring 'weak' virtual agents that evoke empathy and behavioral reflection using social learning theory and virtual self-modeling.
